domains_and_motifs.name: Signal peptide
domains_and_motifs.description: N-terminal signal sequence for membrane targeting and processing. Likely cleaved during maturation based on structural studies showing constructs beginning around residue 70.

sources.notes: Predicted signal peptide; exact cleavage site inferred from structural studies

domains_and_motifs.name: Frizzled cysteine-rich domain
domains_and_motifs.description: Extracellular cysteine-rich domain (CRD) containing ~120 residues with 10 conserved cysteine residues. Primary binding site for WNT ligands. The disulfide bonds form a spherical structure characteristic of the Frizzled family.

domains_and_motifs.name: Frizzled domain core
domains_and_motifs.description: Core Frizzled domain within the CRD responsible for WNT ligand recognition and specificity. Contains critical residues for WNT binding affinity.

domains_and_motifs.name: Hinge domain
domains_and_motifs.description: Linker/hinge domain connecting the extracellular CRD to the transmembrane core. Critical for propagating conformational changes during signal transduction from WNT binding to receptor activation.

domains_and_motifs.name: Transmembrane helix 1
domains_and_motifs.description: First transmembrane helix of the seven-transmembrane GPCR-like architecture

domains_and_motifs.name: Amphipathic helix 8
domains_and_motifs.description: C-terminal amphipathic helix (H8) following TM7, characteristic of GPCRs. Important for membrane association and G protein coupling.

domains_and_motifs.name: PDZ domain binding motif
domains_and_motifs.description: Conserved KTXXXW motif at C-terminus that binds to the PDZ domain of Dishevelled (DVL) proteins. This interaction is critical for canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway activation. The lysine and tryptophan residues are invariant and essential for binding.

sources.notes: The KT...W motif binds DVL PDZ domain with ~7-10 μM affinity

domains_and_motifs.name: N-terminal disordered region
domains_and_motifs.description: N-terminal intrinsically disordered protein region preceding the structured CRD. May be involved in regulatory interactions or post-translational modifications.

sources.notes: Identified as intrinsically disordered region in structural studies

domains_and_motifs.name: Linker disordered region
domains_and_motifs.description: Intrinsically disordered region linking the CRD to the transmembrane domain. Provides flexibility for domain movements during activation.

sources.notes: Identified as intrinsically disordered region in structural studies

experimental_structures.description: Cryo-EM structure of inactive FZD1 in complex with anti-BRIL Fab and nanobody (VHH). Reveals the inactive conformation of the receptor and the structural organization of the transmembrane domain, hinge domain, and amphipathic helix H8.

Cryo-EM structure of FZD1 in complex with mini-Gq protein in the ligand-free state. Shows the active G protein-coupled conformation revealing the framework for Frizzled-G protein coupling and activation mechanisms.

alphafold_prediction.confidence_summary: AlphaFold prediction available for full-length FZD1. Confidence likely high for structured domains (CRD, transmembrane helices) and lower for disordered regions (N-terminus, linker regions).

post_translational_modifications.function: Phosphorylation maintains Frizzled receptors at the plasma membrane. Dvl1 promotes Fzd hyperphosphorylation. Regulated by PCP pathway components including Celsr3 and Vangl2.
post_translational_modifications.evidence: Experimental - studies on Frizzled family members including FZD1

post_translational_modifications.residue: K (multiple lysine residues in cytoplasmic loops)
post_translational_modifications.function: Inhibitory - promotes receptor internalization and degradation. Mediated by E3 ubiquitin ligases ZNRF3 and RNF43. RNF43 preferentially targets FZD1. Negatively regulates Wnt signaling by reducing cell surface receptor levels.
post_translational_modifications.evidence: Experimental - ZNRF3/RNF43 ubiquitinate Frizzled receptors including FZD1

post_translational_modifications.residue: Between signal peptide and mature protein
post_translational_modifications.function: Processing - removal of N-terminal signal peptide during protein maturation and membrane insertion
post_translational_modifications.evidence: Predicted based on signal peptide prediction and structural studies

function.uniprot_function: Receptor for Wnt proteins. FZD1 is a member of the frizzled gene family encoding 7-transmembrane domain proteins that function as receptors in the Wnt signaling pathway. Most frizzled receptors are coupled to the beta-catenin canonical signaling pathway, which leads to activation of disheveled proteins, inhibition of GSK-3 kinase, nuclear accumulation of beta-catenin, and activation of Wnt target genes. FZD1 is activated by WNT3A, WNT3, WNT1 and to a lesser extent WNT2, but apparently not by WNT4, WNT5A, WNT5B, WNT6, WNT7A or WNT7B. Functions in both canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling and non-canonical pathways.
function.catalytic_activity: Not applicable - FZD1 is a receptor, not an enzyme
function.tissue_specificity: Low tissue specificity - expressed across many tissue types. Enhanced expression in retinal horizontal cells, cholangiocytes, peritubular myoid cells, basal prostatic cells, pituicytes/FSCs, and breast secretory cells. Expressed in adult heart, placenta, lung, kidney, pancreas, prostate, ovary, and in fetal lung and kidney.

reactome.pathway_name: TCF dependent signaling in response to WNT
Degradation of beta-catenin by the destruction complex

pathways.pathway_role_summary: FZD1 is a primary receptor for WNT ligands in the canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway. Upon WNT binding, FZD1 cooperates with LRP5/6 co-receptors to recruit DVL proteins, which inhibit the beta-catenin destruction complex. This leads to beta-catenin stabilization, nuclear translocation, and TCF/LEF-dependent gene transcription. FZD1 also participates in non-canonical Wnt signaling through G protein (Gq/G11) coupling. Negatively regulated by ZNRF3/RNF43 E3 ubiquitin ligases and positively regulated by R-spondin proteins. Critical for development, stem cell maintenance, and dysregulated in various cancers.

disease_associations.description: FZD1 is damaged in some colorectal cancer samples and shows pathogenic or disease-associated alterations. Wnt pathway dysregulation is common in colorectal cancer.
Diseases associated with FZD1 include omodysplasia, a skeletal dysplasia disorder.
FZD1 variants and expression changes associated with bone density and osteoporosis risk. Wnt/FZD1 signaling important for osteoblast differentiation.
FZD1 alterations observed in fallopian tube cancers
FZD1 alterations in gastric cancers; target in clinical trials for malignant solid tumors
Wnt5b/FZD1/LRP6 signaling drives renal fibrosis through canonical beta-catenin pathway activation in fibroblasts under hypoxia

metadata.data_quality_notes: Comprehensive data available for FZD1. High-quality cryo-EM structures available (inactive and Gq-coupled states). Quantitative binding data available for WNT3A interaction. Some post-translational modification sites not precisely mapped. Signal peptide cleavage site predicted based on structural data rather than direct experimental determination. Interaction data well-supported by multiple databases and structural studies. Disease associations primarily from cancer genomics data.
metadata.modeling_relevance_summary: FZD1 is a critical Wnt pathway receptor essential for canonical beta-catenin signaling. Key modeling considerations: (1) WNT3A binding affinities measured (Kd ~15 nM); (2) DVL recruitment through C-terminal PDZ motif (~7-10 μM affinity); (3) LRP6 co-receptor complex formation required for signaling; (4) Negative regulation by ZNRF3/RNF43 ubiquitination and positive regulation by RSPOs; (5) G protein coupling (Gq/G11) for non-canonical signaling; (6) Membrane localization subject to regulation by phosphorylation and ubiquitination. Quantitative kinetic data available for WNT3A binding enables parameter estimation. FZD1 acts as both ligand sensor and signal transducer, making it a critical node in Wnt pathway models.
